newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain storm damages wheat, seen moving inland.
newsitem.headline: Spain storm damages wheat, seen moving inland.

text.p: Freak winds of up to 100 kilometres per hour and scattered hail hit the north of Spain on Tuesday, killing one and causing damage to local cereal crops in the Catalan province of Lleida, the civil protection agency said.
Gusts of up to 75 km per hour are forecast to hit the barley-growing region of Castille-La Mancha on Wednesday, the national weather service said.
The area produced around 2.7 million tonnes of Spain's total 10.7 tonne barley crop last year, according to official data.
Local farmers' associations estimated that about 60 percent of the winter cereal crop in Lleida had been damaged by hailstorms which started late Monday. Peach and pear orchards also suffered damage.
Lleida produced about 650,000 tonnes of cereals in 1996, primarily soft wheat.
In Barcelona, a 37-year old woman was killed on Tuesday in when part of an old building's facade in the city centre was dislodged by the strong winds.
In the northwestern region of Galicia, rough sea conditions forced fishing fleets to stay docked at ports.
